domain_findings.narrative: Awesome Go lists Gin as a 'Curated Go library in Web Frameworks' and pkg.go.dev's own package page records it as <cite index="16-8,16-9,16-10">Published: Feb 28, 2026 ... Imports: 44 ... Imported by: 183,243</cite>, indicating both very broad downstream adoption and a release within the last several months.
domain_findings.selection_basis: Featured first/top entry in Awesome Go's Web Frameworks category.

domain_findings.narrative: Cobra is described on its own package page as <cite index="33-1">Package cobra is a commander providing a simple interface to create powerful modern CLI interfaces.</cite> Downstream Linux distribution packaging shows a multi-year, multi-version maintenance trail (Debian sid carrying cobra 1.10.1 alongside older 1.6.1/1.8.1 builds), corroborating sustained upstream releases rather than a one-off snapshot.
domain_findings.selection_basis: The dominant CLI-framework entry cross-referenced by an independent curated Go-modules list.

domain_findings.narrative: The assert subpackage page records <cite index="27-10,27-11,27-12">Published: Aug 17, 2026 ... Imports: 21 ... Imported by: 16,016</cite> and the mock subpackage records <cite index="26-2,26-3,26-4">Published: Aug 17, 2026 ... Imports: 13 ... Imported by: 36,354</cite>, showing both a very recent release and extremely wide reuse across the Go ecosystem.
domain_findings.selection_basis: Top curated Test-Framework entry, also the de facto standard referenced across Go tooling documentation (e.g. testifylint integration with golangci-lint).

domain_findings.narrative: An independent curated module catalogue groups <cite index="34-1">{"zap", "go.uber.org/zap", Tags{LOGGING}}</cite> alongside logrus and zerolog as the established logging options, confirming domain coverage; recency/import-count data for this specific package was not separately retrieved in this session and is treated as a lighter-weight coverage signal only.
domain_findings.selection_basis: Logging entry featured in an independently curated cross-domain Go module catalogue alongside logrus and zerolog.

domain_findings.narrative: The same curated catalogue lists <cite index="34-1">{"gorm", "github.com/go-gorm/gorm", Tags{ORM}}</cite> as the representative ORM package for Go, confirming domain availability; this is a lighter-weight coverage-only signal, not a maintenance-recency signal.
domain_findings.selection_basis: ORM entry featured in the same independently curated cross-domain Go module catalogue.

domain_findings.narrative: The core aws subpackage page shows <cite index="45-3,45-4,45-5">Published: Sep 4, 2026 ... Imports: 15 ... Imported by: 17,424</cite>, and the top-level module page notes <cite index="41-13">The v2 SDK requires a minimum version of Go 1.24.</cite> The predecessor aws-sdk-go v1 page confirms an active, planned sunset rather than silent abandonment: <cite index="43-11">We previously announced our end-of-support plan for AWS SDK for Go (v1).</cite>
domain_findings.selection_basis: Official vendor-maintained SDK, the currently recommended AWS SDK generation for Go per AWS's own successor guidance to aws-sdk-go v1.

evidence.ecosystem_infrastructure_signal: pkg.go.dev itself, the canonical Go package index, continues to receive active investment: the Google Open Source Blog reports <cite index="8-3,8-4">While we initially prioritized providing this comprehensive access via a web interface, the need for streamlined programmatic access has become increasingly clear.</cite> and that a formal v1beta API was shipped in mid-2026, indicating the ecosystem's discovery/tooling layer is actively maintained, not stagnant.
evidence.limitations_of_proxies_used: pkg.go.dev 'Imported by' counts and publish timestamps are used here only as one of several declared evidence lines (alongside independent curated-list inclusion and, for two packages, distro packaging history), never as the sole basis for either metric. 'Imported by' counts favor long-established packages and can undercount usage that occurs via vendoring, private modules, or forks; publish timestamps reflect the latest tagged release of the specific subpackage queried, which can differ slightly from the module's overall latest tag. Two of the six sampled domains (logging, ORM) were only corroborated via curated-list inclusion in this session and lack a directly retrieved recency/import-count figure, which is disclosed as a coverage gap rather than smoothed over.
evidence.package_ecosystem_activity_maintenance_r: Of the four domains where direct pkg.go.dev metadata was retrieved (web framework, testing/mocking, CLI distro trail, cloud SDK), three show a tagged release within roughly the last one to seven months of the snapshot date (Gin: Feb 28, 2026; testify assert/mock: Aug 17, 2026; aws-sdk-go-v2 aws: Sep 4, 2026), and the fourth (Cobra) shows a multi-year cadence of distro-packaged releases (1.6.1 to 1.10.1). The AWS SDK v1-to-v2 transition further shows the ecosystem actively communicating deprecation/successor paths rather than leaving abandoned packages silently in place. The score is not higher because two sampled domains (logging, ORM) lack a directly retrieved recency data point in this session, and because the maintenance sample, though predeclared and reproducible, covers 6 of many possible domains.

predeclared_sampling.candidate_universe: Curated category list at https://awesome-go.com/ (Awesome Go, the community-maintained curated index referenced by go.dev's own ecosystem guidance) crossed with per-package metadata on pkg.go.dev (the official Go package index, data sourced from proxy.golang.org).
predeclared_sampling.retrieval_route: web_search tool against pkg.go.dev package pages, awesome-go.com category pages, and vendor GitHub/release pages; same route and depth used for every sampled domain.
predeclared_sampling.selection_rule: For each predeclared domain, the target library is the package most prominently featured for that domain on the Awesome Go curated list (a language-neutral, benchmark-independent external curation), used as the frozen target before evidence collection. pkg.go.dev is then used only to retrieve that already-selected package's publish recency and 'Imported by' count, never to re-pick a different package after the fact.
predeclared_sampling.snapshot_time: 2026-09-22 (session date; underlying pages carry their own last-updated timestamps, cited per domain below)

evidence.third_party_library_availability_domain_: Across all 6 predeclared domains, Go has at least one library that is both externally curated as the domain's leading option (Awesome Go / independent module catalogues) and, where checked, carries very large downstream adoption (16k-183k importers on pkg.go.dev). No sampled domain lacked a mature, actively distributed option; the score is not 100 because two of six domains (logging, ORM) were confirmed only via curated-list presence rather than a directly retrieved recency/import-count figure in this session, and because the sample, while predeclared and domain-neutral, remains a 6-domain slice rather than an exhaustive audit.
